title: DLite: History-free Speculative Decoding for Agentic AI
abstract: arXiv:2610.23787v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speculative decoding has become a mainstream technique for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference by using a lightweight draft model to generate candidate tokens that are subsequently verified by the target model. However, agentic workloads introduce long and continuously evolving contexts and frequent multi-turn interactions. Under such workloads, we observe that existing draft models suffer from up to an 80% degradation in acceptance length, while maintaining their historical KV cache introduces substantial system overhead. In this paper, we identify the growing historical context as a common source of both problems and introduce DLite, a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI. translated_title: DLite：面向智能体AI的无历史推测解码
translated_abstract: 推测解码已成为加速大语言模型（LLM）推理的主流技术，其通过轻量级草稿模型生成候选token，再由目标模型进行验证。然而，智能体工作负载带来了长且不断演变的上下文以及频繁的多轮交互。在这类工作负载下，我们观察到现有草稿模型的接受长度出现高达80%的性能退化，同时维护历史KV缓存会引入显著的系统开销。在本文中，我们识别出不断增长的历史上下文是这两个问题的共同根源，并提出了DLite——一个面向智能体AI的无历史推测解码框架。DLite直接复用目标模型的上下文隐藏状态，在无需显式维护历史上下文的情况下执行局部推测预测，从而将日益复杂的建模问题转化为局部（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: DLite提出了一种面向智能体AI的无历史推测解码框架，通过直接复用目标模型的上下文隐藏状态进行局部推测预测，无需维护历史KV缓存，从而解决了现有草稿模型在长上下文、多轮交互场景下接受长度退化高达80%及系统开销过大的问题。
en_tdlr: DLite is a history-free speculative decoding framework for agentic AI that directly reuses contextual hidden states from the target model for local speculative prediction, eliminating the need to maintain historical KV caches and addressing up to 80% acceptance length degradation in long-context, multi-turn agentic workloads.
